title: wz run-time configuration
description: The policies and limits a document may state when a node opens or while it runs. A policy the build fixes, a limit only the build sizes, and a limit no machine of the build reads from a statement are not here.

profile.description: The profile the document starts from: a named set of policy values the build declares, which the document's own policies override.

multicast-loopback.description: Whether a datagram a node sends to a multicast group is also delivered to members of that group on the same host.

tx-no-progress-deadline.description: Whether a blocking message gets a second bound beside its total wait: the wait with no progress.

tx-expiry-keeps-session.description: What happens when a blocking message finds no room within its deadline.

declaration-sync-pacing.description: How a node tells a peer its declarations again after a reconnect.
declaration-sync-pacing.x-wz-boundary: the start of the next replay of declarations

datagram-fragment-pacing.description: How fast the fragments of one large message leave a UDP link, unicast or multicast.

multicast-link-requires-iface.description: Whether a multicast link may be opened without an interface the locator chose.

reliable-gap-reconnect.description: What a node does when a frame on the reliable channel arrives with a sequence number that jumped forward, which means frames were lost on the way.

entity-link-restriction.description: Whether an entity may be declared with a set of links it is limited to.

targeted-query.description: Whether a query may be addressed to one peer by its node identity.

publisher-admission-retry.description: Whether a publish may state a bounded retry for the case where no link took it.

multi-route-atomic-tx.description: Whether a publish may ask to be delivered to all of the links it reaches or to none.

entity-timestamp-opt-in.description: What an entity does with a timestamp when its declaration says nothing.

reply-auto-timestamp.description: What a queryable's reply carries when its handler gave it no timestamp.

subscriber-overload.description: What a subscriber whose callback runs off the receive path does when its delivery lane is full and its declaration says nothing.

key-set.description: Which keys the receive path takes a message on (the closed key set).

sn-resolution.description: The width of the sequence numbers the sessions of the C interfaces advertise when their configuration states none: in the InitSyn of a unicast session, where the two sides take the smaller of the two advertised widths, and in the Join of a multicast group, where a member refuses a Join that states another width than its own, so every member of a group states the same.

supervision-after-expiry.description: What a checkpoint does when it is fed after its deadline was missed.

e2e-supervision-notify.description: What a reception supervisor tells the application when a stream stops arriving.

replay-reply-shape.description: How a publisher's replay cache answers a query.

replay-serve-holds-sends.description: Whether a publisher's sends of a message wait while its replay cache answers a query.

replay-live-before-answer.description: How a subscriber that asks for a replay orders its live samples against it.

event-ring-full.description: Which event a full event ring gives up.
event-ring-full.x-wz-boundary: after the consumer has read every record

clock-quality-stamping.description: Whether a node stamps data with a time it does not trust.

routing-face-drive.description: How a node that routes for others serves its links.

routing-table-sharing.description: How a node that routes for others shares its routing tables between the links that route by them and the changes made to them.

reassembly-pool-overflow.description: What a node does with the first fragment of a new fragmented message when every slot of its reassembly pool holds a message still arriving.

link-tie-order.description: How a node orders two zids when it and a peer dialled each other at the same moment and both ends must keep the same one of the two links: the link the node with the lower zid dialled is kept, and this says which zid is lower.

query-unanswerable-final.description: How a node answers a query from a peer that it cannot run at all because the query's key names an id the peer never declared to this node.

zid-derivation.description: How a node makes its zid when the configuration states none.

handshake-stray-message.description: What a unicast establishment does with an Init or an Open that is not the message its current step awaits: an InitAck repeated after the OpenSyn went out, an InitSyn repeated after the InitAck went out, or any other out of its step.

handshake-cookie.description: What cookie a node puts in the InitAck of a link it accepts, and what it takes back.

key-wire-form.description: How a node names a key on the wire to the peer of a link.

MAX_KEYEXPR_BYTES.description: The longest key expression, in bytes, a session stores: a subscription's pattern, or a key a peer declared.

KEY_ARENA_BYTES.description: How many bytes of key text the rows of a session's tables hold at once, in one arena each row keeps its key in: the session's own declarations, the application's tables, its pending gets and what each peer declares to it.

MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS.description: The subscribers a session holds at once.

MATCH_MEMO_SLOTS.description: How many distinct keys the receive match cache remembers at once: the keys whose matching subscriptions it can answer without matching again.

DELIVERY_LANE_EVENTS.description: How many samples the delivery lane of an offloaded subscriber holds at once: the samples the receive path has copied in and its callback has not yet run on.

DELIVERY_LANE_BYTES.description: How many bytes of copied samples a delivery lane holds at once: the key, the payload, the attachment and the encoding schema of each waiting sample, the ids of the subscribers a sample written once for several of them is for, and the end of the byte area a sample skipped to stay in one piece.

DELIVERY_LANE_CALLBACKS.description: How many callback invocations a delivery lane owes at once.

MAX_QUERYABLES.description: The queryables a session holds at once.

MAX_PENDING_QUERIES.description: The queries (gets) a session has waiting for their replies at once.

LINK_NOTED_REQUESTS.description: How many queries a peer sent over one link the node remembers the key form of at once, so that its replies name the key as the query did, when the link names keys by the shared key ids.

MAX_DECL_OBSERVERS.description: The observers an application installs on the declarations of its peers (subscribers, queryables and liveliness tokens appearing or leaving), per kind and per direction.

MAX_LIVELINESS_SUBSCRIPTIONS.description: The liveliness subscribers a session holds at once.

MAX_LOCAL_TOKENS.description: The liveliness tokens a session itself declares and holds at once.

MAX_PUBLISHERS.description: The publishers a session holds at once, each with the write filter that asks whether anything subscribes to its key.

MAX_QUERIERS.description: The queriers a session holds at once, each with the write filter that asks whether anything answers on its key.

MAX_MATCHING_LISTENERS.description: The matching listeners a session holds at once, over all its publishers and queriers.

MAX_DECLARED_KEYEXPRS.description: The key expressions a session declares to its peers at once, each held by the entities that name it and by the program's declarations.

MAX_PENDING_LIVELINESS_GETS.description: The liveliness gets (snapshots of the tokens alive) a session has waiting for their answer at once.

MAX_PENDING_DECLARES.description: The declarations a session can have ready to send in answer to its peers' interests between two sends: each answer is the session's matching declarations and a final.

MAX_INBOUND_SUB_INTERESTS.description: The peers' interests in this session's subscribers that the session remembers, so that a subscriber declared later is announced to them: one per publisher a peer holds with a write filter.

MAX_PEER_KEYEXPR_ALIASES.description: The key expressions one peer may have declared to this session at a time, to name them by a short id.

MAX_SHARED_KEY_IDS.description: The entries of the key-id dictionary every node of a deployment shares (shared-key-ids) that one session may be given.

MAX_REMOTE_DECLS.description: The declarations of one kind (subscribers, queryables, liveliness tokens) one peer may hold open to this session at a time.

MAX_PENDING_REPLIES.description: The replies a session's queryables may have ready to send between two sends.

MAX_PENDING_FINALS.description: The queries a session may owe the end of an answer between two sends.

MAX_REPLY_PAYLOAD_BYTES.description: The largest payload of one reply, in bytes, and the largest attachment beside it.

MAX_MULTICAST_REPLIES.description: The replies a node holds for a multicast group before it sends them, with or without an allocator.

MAX_LOCATOR_LEN.description: The longest locator, in bytes, a node stores: one it is told to connect to, or one it listens on (for example udp/192.168.1.10:7447).

MAX_STATIC_CONNECT.description: The locators a node is told to connect to.

MAX_FACES.description: The faces a session that listens holds besides the one it dials: the links it accepts, those still in their handshake among them, and those it attaches.

MAX_ACCEPT_PENDING.description: The inbound links a session that listens holds in their handshake at once.

QUERIER_MAX_PENDING_QUERIES.description: The queries one declared querier may have in flight at once; one more is refused until a pending one ends.

TX_NO_PROGRESS_WINDOW_US.description: How long, in microseconds, a blocking message may wait with no progress when the tx-no-progress-deadline policy is on: no fragment of it going out.

TX_EXPIRY_CLOSE_AFTER.description: How many blocking messages in a row may find no room within their deadline before the session is closed as unresponsive, when the tx-expiry-keeps-session policy is on.

DATAGRAM_FRAGMENT_BURST.description: How many fragments of a message a UDP link's writer writes in a row when the datagram-fragment-pacing policy is on, before the next one waits for DATAGRAM_FRAGMENT_GAP_US.

DATAGRAM_FRAGMENT_GAP_US.description: How long, in microseconds, must pass after the last fragment was written before a UDP link's writer writes another one past the burst, when the datagram-fragment-pacing policy is on.

QUERY_PARAMETERS_MAX_BYTES.description: The most bytes of selector parameters a query from a peer may carry for this node to run it.

QUERY_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES.description: The most bytes of attachment a query from a peer may carry for this node to run it.

PICO_TX_QUEUE_SIZE.description: How many batches each priority's outbound queue holds for the pico C ABI, in 1 to 16 (upstream's range for a queue size; a value outside it counts as the nearest end).

SNAPSHOT_PERIOD_MS.description: How often, in milliseconds, the node takes a snapshot of itself: what it spends and how its messages are spaced.

SUPERVISION_CHECKPOINTS.description: How many checkpoints the node's supervisor watches.

E2E_SUPERVISED_STREAMS.description: How many periodic streams one reception supervisor holds.

APP_LINK_QUEUE_BYTES.description: The most bytes one link of a transport the program supplies queues in either direction: what the program handed in and the session has not read, and what a session that cannot wait handed over and the program has not taken.

REPLAY_DEPTH_MAX.description: The deepest replay a message may keep: how many of the frames it last sent, as they were sent, a publisher holds for a subscriber that arrives later and asks for them.

MESSAGE_CATALOG_ENTRIES.description: How many messages one message catalog declares, when the message-catalog capability is on.

CLOCK_MAX_FORWARD_STEP_MS.description: How far ahead of the node's clock, in milliseconds, a timestamp from another node may be before the node's hybrid logical clock refuses it, as zenoh's UHLC_MAX_DELTA_MS.

DECLARATION_SYNC_BURST_MESSAGES.description: How many declarations one turn of a paced declaration replay sends, when the declaration-sync-pacing policy is on.

DECLARATION_SYNC_FINAL_TIMEOUT_MS.description: How long, in milliseconds, a node waits for the peer's answer to an interest it sent before it counts the interest as unanswered and goes on.

DECLARATION_SYNC_INTERVAL_MS.description: How long, in milliseconds, a paced declaration replay waits between two of its turns, when the declaration-sync-pacing policy is on.

DECLARATION_SYNC_RX_NO_PROGRESS_MS.description: How long, in milliseconds, a session waits for the next of its peer's initial declarations before it takes the declaration sync as cut short, when the reliable-gap-reconnect policy is not off.

DECLARATION_SYNC_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS.description: How long, in milliseconds, a paced declaration replay waits before it tries again a turn the link did not take for want of room, when the declaration-sync-pacing policy is on.

DECLARATION_SYNC_TX_NO_PROGRESS_MS.description: How long, in milliseconds, a paced declaration replay that retries refused turns (DECLARATION_SYNC_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS not 0) goes on with no declaration sent before it gives up, which ends the link as a refused turn does without retries.

PICO_UNICAST_BATCH_BYTES.description: The batch size, in bytes, a session of the zenoh-pico interface advertises when it opens a unicast session, as zenoh-pico's BATCH_UNICAST_SIZE.

PICO_MULTICAST_BATCH_BYTES.description: The batch size, in bytes, a session of the zenoh-pico interface advertises in the Join of a multicast group, as zenoh-pico's BATCH_MULTICAST_SIZE.

PICO_LEASE_MS.description: The lease, in milliseconds, a session of the zenoh-pico interface advertises, unicast and in a multicast group's Join, as zenoh-pico's Z_TRANSPORT_LEASE.

PICO_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS.description: How long, in milliseconds, one read step of the cooperative zenoh-pico session waits on its link before it returns with nothing, as zenoh-pico's Z_CONFIG_SOCKET_TIMEOUT.

PICO_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS.description: How long, in milliseconds, each open of an endpoint by a zenoh-pico session waits for the dial and the handshake before it fails, on either engine, as zenoh-pico's Z_TRANSPORT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT.

PICO_FRAG_MAX_BYTES.description: The largest message, in bytes, a session of the zenoh-pico interface rejoins from fragments, unicast and in a multicast group, as zenoh-pico's FRAG_MAX_SIZE.

PICO_ACCEPT_TIMEOUT_MS.description: How long, in milliseconds, a listening session of the zenoh-pico interface gives an inbound link to complete its whole handshake, link handshake included, before it drops the link without a word, as zenoh-pico's Z_TRANSPORT_ACCEPT_TIMEOUT.

PICO_KEEPALIVES_PER_LEASE.description: How many keepalives a session of the zenoh-pico interface sends in one lease, as zenoh-pico's Z_TRANSPORT_LEASE_EXPIRE_FACTOR: whenever the line has been idle for the adopted lease divided by this, the session sends one.

key-ids.description: The key ids every node of a deployment shares (the shared-key-ids capability): a dictionary of key expressions by id, and the key-wire form of an endpoint stated apart from the session's.
